name: Elrus
slug: Elrus is Walker's hidden ally in the coming confrontation.
description: Elrus is an ally of Walker who has agreed to accompany him when asked.

log.summary: Walker plans to bring Elrus to The Reach to scout the Dragon Rider training grounds. Walker has promised Elrus a place to stay and considers him a secret weapon who should remain unknown to the lich until the eventual confrontation. Walker expects Elrus to fight Grixto if they encounter him, though he worries Elrus may not hold back. Before departing, Elrus wished the party fruitful ventures and hoped their next meeting would allow them to vanquish their common foe.
notes: Walker stated that he needs to take Elrus somewhere.

log.summary: Elrus travels with Walker and Plymouth toward the Dragon Rider training grounds, having earlier advised that dragon flight from Last Word Chasm to the site takes about five days. He cannot relieve Walker's daily exhaustion, avoids supply runs in Sunder, and helps teach Walker rudimentary fire signals before the group splits. Elrus then flies into the mountains with Araden, planning to rendezvous with the others later.

log.summary: With Araden, Elrus helped end Grixto's group after Grixto killed the guild dragons at the training grounds. He travels with Walker to the training island and speaks into Walker's mind while the wind howls. He identifies the crumbled structure as the guild hall and suspects Grixto's cavern is reached from the backside or underneath. He offers to enter the crack or act as a relay, then stays outside as the relay. Because flag signals need line of sight, he tells Walker to call mentally, and says he can intervene faster than Araden, who would take a long time to dig the crevice open. When Walker contacts him from inside, he asks if Walker is in trouble. He says there has not been a trainee in centuries, that only one person used this place, that he did not know it was there until the vision Walker's friend presented, and that nothing dead should be down there. He agrees to get Plymouth and come down shortly.
notes: With Araden, he brought about the end of Grixto's group after Grixto killed the guild dragons at the training grounds.

log.summary: In Reach legend Elrus killed Galixtar as a trainer without his own legends, contemporary with Garixto the Betrayer, and later a legendary dragon rider. Carlkin does not remember if he was elf or human; some versions say he is still around. Walker called him in; he scrambled down the passage, said nothing to Vecna, with his sword in his belt, stared him down, and kept a side eye on him while leaving. Vecna took him for another of Walker's comrades. Elrus does not want Walker dealing with Vecna and calls the sister story morbid. He reads the four wall carvings as tilted cardinal views from the old central tower, cites mountains about ten and twenty-five degrees off, attributes them to Grixto's faulty memory, and cannot fit the angles to one vantage. He leads Walker from the cavern up a winding half-path across the plains to his and Grixto's ruined guild stronghold. He confirms madness is the most common outcome when a dragon or rider dies, and that he would then seek a book to bring the other back. He treats Walker's Galixtar theory as a real motive for the Al Kurin, better than most he has heard.
notes: In Reach legend he killed Galixtar. At the time he was a trainer without legends of his own, in the same era as Garixto the Betrayer, and he later became a legendary dragon rider. Carlkin does not remember whether he was elf or human. Some versions say he is still around.

Walker told him to come in. He is heard scrambling down the passage. During the talk with Vecna he says nothing, stands with his sword in his belt, and stares Vecna down, then keeps a side eye on him while leaving. Vecna takes him for another of Walker's comrades. He does not want Walker to deal with Vecna and calls the sister story morbid.

Reads the four wall carvings as local cardinal views from the old central tower, each slightly tilted, as if the artist had shifted location while standing in the same spot. He cites mountains about ten and about twenty-five degrees off, attributes the carvings to Grixto working from a faulty memory, and cannot make the angles fit one vantage.

Leads Walker from the cavern up a winding half-path, across the plains, to the ruined guild stronghold of his and Grixto's past. He confirms that madness is the most common outcome when a dragon or its rider dies, and that in that state he himself would seek a book to bring the other back. He treats Walker's theory about Galixtar as a real motive for the Al Kurin, better than most theories he has heard.
